Mathematical wrongness alone is insufficient—there must be textual evidence of the specific error.\n\n---\n\n## The Eight Codes (Disambiguation Order: Highest to Lowest Precedence)\n\n### 1. `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` (Highest Priority)\n**Trigger:** No identifiable final 131-character P/N string.\n- Loops infinitely or appears to (repeated \"thinking\" without conclusion)\n- Truncates mid-classification (stops at pile size 67 with \"...\")\n- Never commits to a concrete string (only describes approach)\n- **Boundary:** Takes precedence over `truncated_or_short_string` when both could apply.\n\n### 2. `wrong_base_case`\n**Trigger:** Classification at pile size 0 is explicitly `N` instead of `P`, OR response states empty pile can still move or wins.\n- Text explicitly claims position 0 is `N`\n- Text claims \"empty pile means you win\" or \"can remove 0 stones\"\n- **Boundary:** Applies specifically to index 0 disagreement. For other positions, use `arithmetic_recursion_error`.\n\n### 3. `pn_convention_swapped`\n**Trigger:** Uses opposite P/N convention where `P` means \"current player wins\" (standard is `P` = previous player wins = current player loses).\n- Explicit reversed definition stated in text: \"P means the player to move wins\"\n- Final string matches bitwise inverse of correct classification\n- **Boundary:** Requires explicit reversed definition OR the inverse pattern is clearly instantiated. Silent wrong answers do not qualify.\n\n### 4. `wrong_loss_convention`\n**Trigger:** Explicitly treats \"last player to move loses\" (misère) or shows inconsistent base case logic.\n- Text states \"taking the last stone loses\"\n- Applies misère logic explicitly\n- Base case logic contradicts standard normal-play convention\n- **Boundary:** Requires explicit misère endorsement or visible inconsistency in loss convention reasoning.\n\n### 5. `truncated_or_short_string`\n**Trigger:** Final string not exactly 131 characters from {P,N}.\n- Wrong length (130 chars, 132 chars)\n- Contains characters other than P or N\n- Split across newlines with whitespace\n- **Boundary:** Check after verifying response actually terminates. Overridden by `non_terminating_or_no_final_string`.\n\n### 6. `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n**Trigger:** Classification rests on unjustified pattern without computing the game tree.\n- \"All even sizes are P\"\n- \"Every 4th position is N\"\n- \"Pattern alternates P/N/P/N\"\n- Claims periodicity without Sprague-Grundy recurrence proof\n- **Boundary:** Pattern-based responses without recurrence setup go here. Must be explicitly stated in text, not inferred from wrong output.\n\n### 7. `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n**Trigger:** Correct recursion setup but per-position computation mistakes.\n- Uses proper Sprague-Grundy recurrence: position k is P iff all k - move are N, and k is N iff exists k - move that is P\n- Correct base case at 0\n- Correct P/N convention\n- But final string is 131 chars with correct convention but wrong individual values\n- **Boundary:** Requires visible correct recursion + base case + convention. If setup is wrong, use other codes.\n\n### 8. `missing_subtraction_moves` (Lowest Priority)\n**Trigger:** Enumerated move set omits one or more legal moves from the union of squares and triangulars up to 130.\n- Lists moves explicitly but omits 36 (both square and triangular)\n- Forgets triangular numbers above 55\n- Only uses squares, omits triangulars entirely (when stated)\n- **Boundary:** Requires concrete enumeration showing incomplete move set. Silence about moves is not sufficient—must see explicit incomplete list or explicit exclusion.\n\n---\n\n## Application Rules\n\n| Scenario | Code to Apply | Rationale |\n|----------|--------------|-----------|\n| Response says \"P means player to move wins\" + has 131 chars | `pn_convention_swapped` | Explicit reversed definition |\n| Response stops at position 85 with \"...\" | `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` | Never committed to complete string |\n| Response says \"0 is N because you can still move\" | `wrong_base_case` | Explicit base case error |\n| Response says \"I notice all even indices are P\" + assigns accordingly | `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic` | Pattern without recursion |\n| Response sets up recurrence correctly but miscalculates position 7 | `arithmetic_recursion_error` | Correct setup, wrong execution |\n| Response lists moves: {1,3,4,6,9,10,15,16,21,25} | `missing_subtraction_moves` | Concrete incomplete enumeration |\n| Response says \"last player to move loses\" | `wrong_loss_convention` | Explicit misère endorsement |\n| Output is 129 characters with \"PNPN...\" | `truncated_or_short_string` | Wrong length |\n| Output trails off mid-string with no conclusion | `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` | Never terminated |\n\n---\n\n## Critical Boundary Clarifications\n\n### Concrete Instantiation Required\n- **YES:** \"The moves are 1, 4, 9, 16...\" (lists moves, can check for omissions)\n- **NO:** Silent omission of triangular numbers (no text to audit)\n- **YES:** \"I see a pattern: P at all multiples of 3\" (explicit heuristic)\n- **NO:** Wrong answer without stated reasoning (cannot infer arbitrary pattern)\n\n### Precedence Overrides\n1. `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` > `truncated_or_short_string`\n2. `wrong_base_case` for index 0 > other codes for index 0\n3. `pn_convention_swapped` requires explicit reversed definition OR inverse string\n4. `wrong_loss_convention` requires explicit misère endorsement\n5. `truncated_or_short_string` for wrong length > pattern/recursion errors\n6. `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic` for unjustified patterns > `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n7. `arithmetic_recursion_error` requires correct recursion + base case + convention\n8. `missing_subtraction_moves` requires concrete enumeration\n\n### Pattern vs. Recursion\n- **Pattern without recurrence →** `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n- **Recurrence attempt with errors →** `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n- **No visible reasoning →** Cannot apply either; check other codes or `non_terminating_or_no_final_string`\n\n### Textual Evidence Standard\nApply a code **only if** you can quote specific text instantiating the trigger condition. Codes are not for inferred mathematical errors—they are for auditable, textual failures.","old_start":1,"new_start":1,"is_summary":false}],"extras":null}}}}}}
